title: GPU loss-history 'iteration' is 0-based int while CPU callback writes 1-based float, mis-aligning the loss-curve x-axis between paths
description: The CPU progress callback (_CatBoostProgressCallback.after_iteration) records `history_entry = {"iteration": float(it)}` with `it = info.iteration + 1` — i.e. 1-based and float. The GPU reconstruction branch in CatBoostAlgorithm.fit (lines 567-581) instead appends `{"iteration": i}` where `i` is the 0-based enumerate index and an int. The two paths therefore emit different `iteration` conventions for the same logical training. render_loss_curve_svg (src/haute/modelling/_charts.py:310/369/378) uses this `iteration` field directly as the x-coordinate (`x_pos(iterations[i])`), and the best-iteration marker is positioned with `x_pos(best_iteration)` (line 386-387) where best_iteration comes from CatBoost's 0-based `best_iteration_`. Consequently the marker is consistent with the curve on GPU (both 0-based) but off-by-one on CPU (curve 1-based, marker 0-based), and the same model trained on CPU vs GPU renders its x-axis shifted by one. The divergence is a contract mismatch between two in-scope code paths writing the same loss_history schema.
evidence: Line 190-194: `it = info.iteration + 1` then `history_entry = {"iteration": float(it)}` (1-based, float). Lines 573-575/579-581: `if i >= len(loss_history): loss_history.append({"iteration": i})` with `for i, v in enumerate(values)` (0-based, int). _charts.py:386 `clamped = min(best_iteration, x_max); bx = x_pos(clamped)` plots best_iteration on the same axis as `iterations` (line 310 `d.get("iteration", i)`), so a 1-based curve + 0-based marker (CPU) is misaligned by one.
